organizations.name: South Florida People of Color
organizations.overview: South Florida People of Color (dba Miami Shores People of Color) is a 501(c)(3) racial healing organization founded in Miami Shores in 2015, running community dialogue programs to dismantle racism through open, personal interaction across racial and ethnic lines.

accomplishments.text: Has run community race-dialogue programming based in Miami Shores for 10 years (since 2015) — Unity360 Community Race Dialogues, Awkward Dinners, Redlining Tours, and a Racial Healing Book Club. The founder credits the group's early organizing on political representation with contributing to Miami Shores electing its first Black mayor three years later — the group's own characterization, not independently verified causation.

plannedActivities.text: Presenting 'Uhuru: Liberation through Education and Cultural Creativity,' a Juneteenth celebration at Barry University on June 19, with a keynote from historian Dr. Tameka Hobbs — their third consecutive year partnering with Barry on the event.

reviewNotes: Two corrections from a follow-up recency check. (1) The mayor-election claim needed care: the source article quotes the founder's own account ('Three years after the first meeting on political representation...Miami Shores got our first Black mayor') without naming the mayor or independently establishing causation — attributed to the founder rather than stated as fact. (2) The Juneteenth item was UPGRADED, not just verified: the original citation only established a recurring pattern ('for the last two years' as of Oct 2025); a follow-up search found the actual named, dated 2026 event with a specific speaker, which is a stronger, more current citation than what first surfaced. Recency checks don't only catch bad claims — they can also replace a vague-but-true one with a specific-and-verified one.
